questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The pars intermedia of the human pituitary gland secretes:

solution.explanation: The adenohypophysis has two parts. The pars distalis (anterior pituitary) secretes GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH, while the pars intermedia secretes only one hormone, melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH).
steps: Pars distalis → GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH
Neurohypophysis → stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin
solution.why_others_wrong: ACTH and prolactin come from the pars distalis; oxytocin is released from the neurohypophysis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: Melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which hormone is called a hypercalcemic hormone because it increases the Ca²⁺ level in the blood?

solution.explanation: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) raises blood Ca²⁺ by stimulating bone resorption (demineralisation), reabsorption of Ca²⁺ by the renal tubules and absorption of Ca²⁺ from digested food. Hence it is a hypercalcemic hormone.
steps: PTH → bone resorption, renal Ca²⁺ reabsorption, intestinal Ca²⁺ absorption
solution.why_others_wrong: Thyrocalcitonin also regulates blood calcium but is not the hormone that raises it; melatonin regulates diurnal rhythm; glucagon is hyperglycemic, not hypercalcemic.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Parathyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: Parathyroid hormone (PTH)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Melatonin, secreted by the pineal gland, plays a very important role in regulating the:

options.text: Level of calcium in the blood
Reabsorption of sodium by the renal tubules
24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body, such as the sleep-wake cycle
Contraction of the uterine muscles during childbirth

solution.explanation: The pineal gland lies on the dorsal side of the forebrain and secretes melatonin, which regulates the 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body, for example the sleep-wake cycle and body temperature.
steps: Melatonin → diurnal (24-hour) rhythms such as sleep-wake cycle
solution.why_others_wrong: Blood calcium is regulated by PTH and TCT, sodium reabsorption by aldosterone, and uterine contraction by oxytocin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pineal gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body, such as the sleep-wake cycle

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Androgens, mainly testosterone, are synthesised and secreted by the:

options.text: Sertoli cells of the seminiferous tubules

solution.explanation: The interstitial spaces of the testis contain Leydig cells (interstitial cells), which produce androgens, mainly testosterone.
steps: Seminiferous tubules: germ cells and Sertoli cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Sertoli cells nourish germ cells; spermatogonia are germ cells; the adrenal medulla secretes catecholamines.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Testis
solution.final_answer: Option D: Leydig (interstitial) cells of the testis

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Insulin acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes and enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation.
Statement II: Insulin is secreted by the α-cells of the islets of Langerhans.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Insulin, a peptide hormone, acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes and moves glucose rapidly from blood into these cells. It is secreted by the β-cells; the α-cells secrete glucagon.
steps: Statement I: true (target cells of insulin)
Statement II: false (insulin from β-cells, glucagon from α-cells)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pancreas
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (pituitary hormone) with List-II (function).

List-I:
A. Prolactin
B. ACTH
C. LH (in males)
D. MSH

List-II:
I. Regulates pigmentation by acting on melanocytes
II. Stimulates synthesis and secretion of androgens from the testis
III. Stimulates synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex
IV. Regulates growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Functions of anterior and intermediate pituitary hormones
solution.explanation: Each pituitary hormone has a defined target: PRL acts on mammary glands, ACTH on the adrenal cortex, LH on the Leydig cells of the testis, and MSH on melanocytes.
steps: Prolactin → mammary gland growth and milk formation → IV
ACTH → glucocorticoids from adrenal cortex → III
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about glucocorticoids are correct?

(a) They stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis.
(b) They inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids.
(c) Their secretion from the adrenal cortex is stimulated by TSH.
(d) Cortisol produces anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response.
(e) Aldosterone is the main glucocorticoid of the body.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Glucocorticoids (mainly cortisol) stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis, inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids, and suppress the immune response. Their secretion is stimulated by ACTH. Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid.
steps: (c) False: ACTH, not TSH, stimulates the adrenal cortex
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing (c) or (e) is wrong: TSH acts on the thyroid, and aldosterone controls Na⁺ and water.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Steroid hormones mostly regulate gene expression or chromosome function in their target cells.
Reason (R): Steroid hormones interact with intracellular receptors, and the hormone-receptor complex interacts with the genome.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Hormones such as steroids and iodothyronines bind intracellular (mostly nuclear) receptors. The hormone-receptor complex interacts with the genome, so these hormones mostly act by regulating gene expression or chromosome function. R therefore explains A.
steps: The hormone-receptor complex acting on the genome is why steroids regulate gene expression
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Mechanism of hormone action
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.
Statement II: Oxytocin and vasopressin are synthesised by the cells of the neurohypophysis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The posterior pituitary is under direct neural control of the hypothalamus. Oxytocin and vasopressin are synthesised by the hypothalamus and transported axonally to the neurohypophysis, which only stores and releases them.
steps: Statement II: false (synthesised in the hypothalamus; neurohypophysis stores and releases)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Hypothalamus; The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A patient shows an enlarged thyroid gland, protruding eyeballs, an increased basal metabolic rate and weight loss. The condition is most likely:

options.text: Cretinism, caused by hypothyroidism during pregnancy
Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease), a form of hyperthyroidism
Simple goitre caused by iodine deficiency
Addison's disease, caused by underproduction of adrenocortical hormones

solution.explanation: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism marked by an enlarged thyroid, protruded eyeballs, increased BMR and weight loss.
steps: Increased BMR and weight loss → excess thyroid hormone (hyperthyroidism)
Enlarged thyroid + protruding eyeballs → exophthalmic goitre
solution.why_others_wrong: Cretinism and iodine-deficiency goitre are hypothyroid states (BMR would not rise); Addison's disease involves the adrenal cortex, not the thyroid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Thyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease), a form of hyperthyroidism

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about androgens are correct?

(a) They regulate the development, maturation and functions of male accessory sex organs such as the epididymis, vas deferens and seminal vesicles.
(b) They inhibit spermatogenesis.
(c) They act on the central nervous system and influence male sexual behaviour (libido).
(d) They have a catabolic effect on protein metabolism.
(e) They stimulate muscular growth and the growth of facial and axillary hair.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Androgens regulate the male accessory sex organs, stimulate muscular growth, facial and axillary hair, aggressiveness and low pitch of voice, play a stimulatory role in spermatogenesis, influence libido through the CNS, and have anabolic effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (b) or (d) reverse the actual effects: androgens are stimulatory for spermatogenesis and anabolic.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Testis
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (hormone) with List-II (chemical nature).

List-I:
A. Insulin
B. Cortisol
C. Thyroxine
D. Epinephrine

List-II:
I. Steroid
II. Amino-acid derivative
III. Peptide/protein hormone
IV. Iodothyronine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT groups hormones as peptide/polypeptide/protein hormones (insulin, glucagon, pituitary and hypothalamic hormones), steroids (cortisol, testosterone, estradiol, progesterone), iodothyronines (thyroid hormones) and amino-acid derivatives (epinephrine).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Mechanism of hormone action
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the hypothalamus and pituitary are correct?

(a) GnRH from the hypothalamus stimulates the pituitary to synthesise and release gonadotrophins.
(b) Somatostatin from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.
(c) Hypothalamic hormones reach the posterior pituitary through a portal circulatory system.
(d) In humans, the pars intermedia is almost merged with the pars distalis.
(e) The neurohypophysis secretes ACTH.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Hypothalamic releasing (e.g. GnRH) and inhibiting (e.g. somatostatin) hormones reach the anterior pituitary through the hypophyseal portal system. The posterior pituitary is under direct neural control. In humans the pars intermedia is almost merged with the pars distalis. ACTH comes from the pars distalis.
steps: (c) False: the portal system serves the anterior pituitary
(e) False: ACTH is an anterior pituitary hormone; the neurohypophysis releases oxytocin and vasopressin
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement (c) is the trap: the portal system links the hypothalamus with the anterior, not the posterior, pituitary.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Hypothalamus; The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Glucagon is a hyperglycemic hormone.
Reason (R): Glucagon stimulates glycogenesis in hepatocytes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Glucagon and insulin have opposite actions
solution.explanation: Glucagon acts on hepatocytes and stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, and reduces cellular glucose uptake, so blood glucose rises: A is true. Glycogenesis (glucose → glycogen) is stimulated by insulin, so R is false.
steps: R: false (glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis; insulin stimulates glycogenesis)
solution.why_others_wrong: Students who confuse glycogenesis with glycogenolysis mark option A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pancreas
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Hormones that interact with membrane-bound receptors normally enter the target cell to bring about their effects.
Statement II: Iodothyronines act mainly through membrane-bound receptors and generate second messengers such as cyclic AMP.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Hormones binding membrane-bound receptors normally do not enter the target cell; they generate second messengers (cyclic AMP, IP₃, Ca²⁺). Iodothyronines, like steroids, interact with intracellular receptors and regulate gene expression. Both statements are false.
steps: Statement I: false (they do not enter the cell)
Statement II: false (iodothyronines use intracellular receptors)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Mechanism of hormone action
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (disorder) with List-II (cause).

List-I:
A. Addison's disease
B. Cretinism
C. Acromegaly
D. Pituitary dwarfism

List-II:
I. Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults, especially in middle age
II. Underproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex
III. Hypothyroidism during pregnancy, affecting the developing baby
IV. Low secretion of growth hormone, resulting in stunted growth

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Addison's disease results from underproduction of adrenocortical hormones (acute weakness, fatigue). Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes cretinism in the baby. Excess GH in adults causes acromegaly; low GH causes pituitary dwarfism.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping acromegaly and dwarfism, or linking cretinism with the adrenal cortex, are the usual errors.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pituitary gland; Thyroid gland; Adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the hormones of the adrenal medulla are correct?

(a) Adrenaline and noradrenaline are rapidly secreted in response to stress of any kind and during emergency situations.
(b) They cause constriction of the pupils.
(c) They increase the heartbeat, the strength of heart contraction and the rate of respiration.
(d) They stimulate the breakdown of glycogen, increasing the glucose concentration in blood.
(e) They are steroid hormones secreted by the zona fasciculata.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The adrenal medulla secretes adrenaline and noradrenaline (catecholamines), the 'fight or flight' hormones. They increase alertness, cause pupillary dilation, piloerection and sweating, raise heart rate, strength of contraction and breathing rate, and stimulate glycogenolysis.
steps: (e) False: catecholamines are amino-acid derivatives from the medulla; zona fasciculata is part of the cortex
solution.why_others_wrong: (b) reverses the effect on the pupil, and (e) confuses the medulla with the cortex.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The scrotum helps to maintain the temperature of the testes lower than the normal internal body temperature, which is necessary for spermatogenesis. The difference is about:

solution.explanation: The testes lie outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum, which keeps them 2–2.5 °C below the normal internal body temperature, as needed for spermatogenesis.
steps: Testes are extra-abdominal, in the scrotum
Scrotal temperature is 2–2.5 °C lower than body temperature
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Male reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option B: 2–2.5 °C

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Within the seminiferous tubules of the testis, the cells that provide nutrition to the germ cells are the:

options.text: Immunocompetent cells of the interstitial spaces

solution.explanation: Each seminiferous tubule is lined by male germ cells (spermatogonia) and Sertoli cells. Sertoli cells provide nutrition to the germ cells.
steps: Lining of seminiferous tubule: spermatogonia + Sertoli cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Leydig cells and immunocompetent cells lie in the interstitial spaces outside the tubules; spermatogonia are the germ cells themselves.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Male reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option C: Sertoli cells

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The funnel-shaped part of the oviduct closer to the ovary, whose edges bear finger-like projections that help in collecting the ovum after ovulation, is the:

solution.explanation: The oviduct (10–12 cm) has three parts: the funnel-shaped infundibulum with fimbriae close to the ovary, the wider ampulla, and the narrow isthmus that joins the uterus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Female reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option D: Infundibulum

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: An embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is called a:

solution.explanation: Mitotic divisions (cleavage) of the zygote give 2, 4, 8, 16 blastomeres. The embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is the morula, which develops further into the blastocyst.
solution.why_others_wrong: The blastocyst comes after the morula; the trophoblast is only the outer layer of the blastocyst.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and implantation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Morula

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The milk produced during the initial few days of lactation is called colostrum.
Statement II: Colostrum contains several antibodies that are essential to develop resistance in new-born babies.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The mammary glands start producing milk towards the end of pregnancy. The milk of the first few days, colostrum, contains several antibodies essential for developing resistance in the new-born. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Parturition and lactation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The first menstruation that begins at puberty is called:

solution.explanation: The first menstruation at puberty is menarche. The cycles cease around 50 years of age; this is menopause.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: Menarche

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: During a coitus, a man ejaculates 250 million sperms. According to NCERT, for normal fertility at least 60% of the sperms must have normal shape and size, and at least 40% of them must show vigorous motility. The minimum number of sperms in this ejaculate that must have normal shape and size is:

solution.explanation: The shape-and-size criterion is the 60% figure and applies to all the sperms ejaculated; the 40% figure is the separate motility criterion.
steps: Normal shape and size needed in ≥ 60% of the sperms
solution.why_others_wrong: 100 million uses the 40% motility figure; 60 million multiplies the two criteria (0.6 × 0.4); 50 million subtracts the two percentages (20%).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis (structure of sperm and sperm count)
solution.final_answer: Option D: 150 million

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (part of the uterus) with List-II (feature).

List-I:
A. Perimetrium
B. Myometrium
C. Endometrium
D. Cervical canal

List-II:
I. Thick layer of smooth muscle that shows strong contractions during delivery of the baby
II. Thin, outer membranous layer
III. Inner glandular layer that undergoes cyclical changes during the menstrual cycle
IV. Together with the vagina, forms the birth canal

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The uterine wall has three layers: the outer thin perimetrium, the middle thick muscular myometrium and the inner glandular endometrium. The uterus opens into the vagina through the cervix; the cervical canal and vagina form the birth canal.
steps: Myometrium → smooth muscle, contractions at delivery → I
Cervical canal + vagina → birth canal → IV
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Female reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the male reproductive system are correct?

(a) Secretions of the accessory glands constitute the seminal plasma, which is rich in fructose, calcium and certain enzymes.
(b) Secretions of the bulbourethral glands help in the lubrication of the penis.
(c) The prostate is a paired gland.
(d) The vas deferens receives a duct from the seminal vesicle and opens into the urethra as the ejaculatory duct.
(e) The epididymis lies along the anterior surface of each testis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The accessory glands are paired seminal vesicles, a single prostate and paired bulbourethral glands. The epididymis lies along the posterior surface of each testis. The vas deferens loops over the urinary bladder, receives the duct of the seminal vesicle and opens into the urethra as the ejaculatory duct.
steps: (e) False: the epididymis is along the posterior surface
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Male reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Not all copulations lead to fertilisation and pregnancy.
Reason (R): Fertilisation can occur only if the ovum and sperms are transported simultaneously to the ampullary region.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Sperms swim through the cervix and uterus to the ampullary region of the fallopian tube, where the ovum is also transported. Fertilisation happens only when both arrive there at the same time. NCERT gives this as the reason why not all copulations lead to fertilisation and pregnancy, so R explains A.
steps: The need for simultaneous arrival at the ampullary region explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and implantation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The second meiotic division of the secondary oocyte is equal and forms two ootids.
Statement II: Entry of the sperm into the ovum induces completion of the meiotic division of the secondary oocyte.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The sperm's entry induces the secondary oocyte to complete meiosis II. This division is unequal, giving a second polar body and a haploid ootid.
steps: Statement I: false (unequal division: second polar body + one ootid)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and implantation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following hormones is produced in women only during pregnancy?

solution.explanation: hCG, hPL and relaxin are produced in women only during pregnancy. Estrogens, progestogens and prolactin are also produced outside pregnancy, though their levels rise several-fold during it.
steps: Estrogen, progesterone, prolactin: increased, but not exclusive
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Pregnancy and embryonic development
solution.final_answer: Option C: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The rupture of the Graafian follicle and the release of the ovum in the middle of the menstrual cycle is induced by:

options.text: A sharp fall in FSH secretion
A rapid surge in LH secretion
Rising progesterone secreted by the corpus luteum

solution.explanation: LH and FSH rise during the follicular phase and peak in mid-cycle. The rapid secretion of LH to its maximum (LH surge) induces rupture of the Graafian follicle and thereby ovulation.
steps: Mid-cycle LH surge → rupture of Graafian follicle → ovulation
solution.why_others_wrong: The corpus luteum forms only after ovulation, and its degeneration leads to menstruation, not ovulation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option B: A rapid surge in LH secretion

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure) with List-II (role).

List-I:
A. Acrosome
B. Middle piece of sperm
C. Zona pellucida
D. Trophoblast

List-II:
I. Gets attached to the endometrium during implantation
II. Contains numerous mitochondria that produce energy for tail movement
III. Cap-like structure filled with enzymes that help in fertilisation
IV. Layer whose changes on sperm contact block the entry of additional sperms

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The acrosome on the sperm head holds enzymes that help the sperm enter the ovum. The middle piece has mitochondria for tail movement. Changes in the zona pellucida after sperm contact block polyspermy. The trophoblast of the blastocyst attaches to the endometrium.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis; Fertilisation and implantation
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: By the end of which period of pregnancy are most of the major organ systems of the human foetus formed, with the limbs and external genital organs well developed?

solution.explanation: Heart forms after one month; limbs and digits by the end of the second month; most major organ systems by the end of 12 weeks (first trimester); first movements and head hair in the fifth month; eyelids separate and eyelashes form by the end of 24 weeks.
steps: End of 12 weeks (first trimester) → most major organ systems formed
solution.why_others_wrong: End of the first month: only the heart has formed. Fifth month: first foetal movements. End of 24 weeks: eyelids separate and eyelashes form.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Pregnancy and embryonic development
solution.final_answer: Option D: End of 12 weeks (first trimester)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a human male, 50 secondary spermatocytes complete spermatogenesis. In a human female, 50 primary oocytes complete oogenesis (assume every secondary oocyte is fertilised, so both meiotic divisions are completed). The number of spermatozoa and of functional female gametes (ova) formed are, respectively:

solution.explanation: A secondary spermatocyte is already past meiosis I; meiosis II gives 2 spermatids, each becoming a sperm. A primary oocyte gives only one functional gamete, because both meiotic divisions are unequal and produce polar bodies.
solution.why_others_wrong: 200 treats secondary spermatocytes as primary ones (4 sperms each); 100 or 200 ova ignores that oogenesis gives one ovum and polar bodies.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option A: 100 and 50

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about oogenesis are correct?

(a) Oogonia are formed within each fetal ovary during embryonic development, and no more oogonia are formed or added after birth.
(b) Primary oocytes enter prophase-I of meiosis and get temporarily arrested at that stage.
(c) A fluid-filled cavity called the antrum first appears in the secondary follicle.
(d) At puberty, only about 60,000–80,000 primary follicles are left in each ovary.
(e) Primary follicles get surrounded by more layers of granulosa cells and a new theca to become secondary follicles.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Oogenesis starts in the fetal ovary; oogonia enter prophase-I and are arrested as primary oocytes. Many follicles degenerate before puberty, leaving 60,000–80,000 primary follicles in each ovary. Primary → secondary follicle (more granulosa layers, new theca) → tertiary follicle with the fluid-filled antrum → Graafian follicle.
steps: (c) False: the antrum characterises the tertiary follicle
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) is the trap: the antrum defines the tertiary follicle, not the secondary follicle.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone.
Reason (R): The corpus luteum is formed from the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle during the follicular phase.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: After ovulation, in the luteal phase, the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle form the corpus luteum, which secretes large amounts of progesterone to maintain the endometrium. A is true; R wrongly places its formation in the follicular phase.
steps: R: false (corpus luteum forms after ovulation, in the luteal phase)
solution.why_others_wrong: The follicular phase comes before ovulation, when the Graafian follicle is still growing.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The signals for parturition originate from the maternal hypothalamus, independently of the foetus.
Statement II: Oxytocin acts on the uterine muscle to cause stronger contractions, which in turn stimulate further secretion of oxytocin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Signals for parturition come from the fully developed foetus and the placenta, which induce mild uterine contractions (foetal ejection reflex). This triggers oxytocin release from the maternal pituitary; oxytocin causes stronger contractions, which stimulate more oxytocin secretion, until the baby is expelled.
steps: Statement I: false (signals from the foetus and placenta)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Parturition and lactation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the human menstrual cycle are correct?

(a) Both LH and FSH attain a peak level in the middle of the cycle (about the 14th day).
(b) During the follicular phase, the endometrium regenerates through proliferation.
(c) Menstruation occurs only if the released ovum is not fertilised.
(d) Lack of menstruation is always an indication of pregnancy.
(e) During pregnancy, all events of the menstrual cycle stop and there is no menstruation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Phases and hormonal control of the menstrual cycle
solution.explanation: LH and FSH peak around day 14. The endometrium regenerates in the follicular phase. Menstruation occurs only when the ovum is not fertilised, and cycles stop during pregnancy. Lack of menstruation may indicate pregnancy, but it may also be caused by stress or poor health.
steps: (d) False: stress or poor health can also stop menstruation
solution.why_others_wrong: The word 'always' makes (d) false; the option with only (b), (c) and (e) leaves out the true statement (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following shows the correct path of sperms from their site of formation to the outside of the body?

options.text: Seminiferous tubules → vasa efferentia → rete testis → epididymis → vas deferens → ejaculatory duct → urethra
Seminiferous tubules → rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens → ejaculatory duct → urethra
Seminiferous tubules → rete testis → epididymis → vasa efferentia → vas deferens → ejaculatory duct → urethra
Seminiferous tubules → rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → ejaculatory duct → vas deferens → urethra

solution.explanation: Sperms formed in the seminiferous tubules pass through the rete testis and vasa efferentia to the epididymis, then the vas deferens, which joins the duct of the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct opening into the urethra.
steps: Seminiferous tubules → rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis
Epididymis → vas deferens → ejaculatory duct → urethra → urethral meatus
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong sequence swaps one adjacent pair: rete testis/vasa efferentia, epididymis/vasa efferentia, or vas deferens/ejaculatory duct.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Male reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option B: Seminiferous tubules → rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens → ejaculatory duct → urethra

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of an ideal contraceptive?

options.text: It should be user-friendly and easily available
It should have no or the least side-effects
It should be irreversible, so that fertility does not return
It should not interfere with the sexual drive, desire or the sexual act

solution.explanation: An ideal contraceptive should be user-friendly, easily available, effective and reversible, with no or least side-effects, and should in no way interfere with the sexual drive, desire or the sexual act.
steps: Ideal = user-friendly, available, effective, reversible, least side-effects, no interference with sexual act
Irreversibility is the opposite of what is required
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population stabilisation and birth control
solution.final_answer: Option C: It should be irreversible, so that fertility does not return

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In vasectomy:

options.text: A small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen
A device is inserted into the uterus through the vagina
A small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum

solution.explanation: Vasectomy is the surgical method in males: a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum, which blocks gamete transport. In tubectomy, a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up.
steps: Male sterilisation → vas deferens cut/tied through scrotal incision
solution.why_others_wrong: The fallopian-tube option describes tubectomy; the device option describes an IUD; sterilisation does not remove the testes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population stabilisation and birth control
solution.final_answer: Option D: A small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Condoms protect the user from STIs and AIDS in addition to preventing conception.
Statement II: Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are single-use devices that cannot be reused.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/latex that also protect against STIs and AIDS. Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are rubber barriers placed over the cervix during coitus; they are reusable.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population stabilisation and birth control
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In intra-uterine insemination (IUI), the semen collected from the husband or a healthy donor is artificially introduced into the:

options.text: Fallopian tube, together with a donor ovum
Ovum, by direct injection of one sperm

solution.explanation: When the male partner cannot inseminate the female or has a very low sperm count, semen is collected and artificially introduced into the vagina or into the uterus. Introduction into the uterus is IUI.
steps: Artificial insemination: semen → vagina or uterus
solution.why_others_wrong: Transfer with a donor ovum into the fallopian tube is GIFT, and injecting a sperm into an ovum is ICSI.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Infertility
solution.final_answer: Option B: Uterus

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (contraceptive) with List-II (category).

List-I:
A. Lippes loop
B. LNG-20
C. Cervical cap
D. Periodic abstinence

List-II:
I. Hormone-releasing IUD
II. Barrier method
III. Non-medicated IUD
IV. Natural method

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: IUDs are non-medicated (Lippes loop), copper-releasing (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) or hormone-releasing (Progestasert, LNG-20). Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are barriers. Periodic abstinence is a natural method.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population stabilisation and birth control
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about oral contraceptive pills are correct?

(a) They contain progestogens or progestogen–estrogen combinations.
(b) They are taken daily for 21 days, starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle.
(c) They make the cervical mucus more favourable for the entry of sperms.
(d) Saheli is a steroidal pill that has to be taken daily.
(e) They inhibit ovulation and implantation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Pills (progestogens alone or with estrogen) are taken daily for 21 days, starting within the first five days of the cycle, then repeated after a 7-day gap. They inhibit ovulation and implantation and alter the cervical mucus to prevent or retard sperm entry. Saheli is a non-steroidal, once-a-week pill.
steps: (c) False: they make the mucus hostile to sperm entry
(d) False: Saheli is non-steroidal and taken once a week
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population stabilisation and birth control
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): As long as a mother breast-feeds her child fully, the chances of conception in the first few months after parturition are almost nil.
Reason (R): Ovulation, and therefore the menstrual cycle, do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Lactational amenorrhea is a natural method based on the absence of ovulation during intense lactation. Because no ovum is released, conception is almost impossible while the mother breast-feeds fully (reported effective up to six months). R explains A.
steps: No ovulation → no ovum to fertilise → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population stabilisation and birth control
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: IUDs decrease the phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus.
Statement II: Hormone-releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus; copper ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity; hormone-releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.
steps: Statement I: false (IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population stabilisation and birth control
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) is considered relatively safe up to:

options.text: 24 weeks (the end of the second trimester) of pregnancy
Any stage of pregnancy, if done by a doctor

solution.explanation: MTPs are considered relatively safe during the first trimester, i.e. up to 12 weeks of pregnancy. Second-trimester abortions are much riskier.
steps: First trimester = up to 12 weeks → relatively safe
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Medical termination of pregnancy (MTP)
solution.final_answer: Option C: 12 weeks (the first trimester) of pregnancy

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about amniocentesis is correct?

options.text: It is legally permitted in India for determining the sex of the foetus
It is based on the chromosomal pattern in the amniotic fluid and can detect genetic disorders such as Down syndrome
It is a technique for transferring an early embryo into the uterus
It detects pregnancy by testing the mother's urine for hCG

solution.explanation: Amniocentesis studies the chromosomal pattern in the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing embryo. It is used to detect genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia and sickle-cell anaemia. Its use for foetal sex determination is banned by law to check female foeticide.
steps: Use: genetic disorders; sex determination is statutorily banned
solution.why_others_wrong: Sex determination by amniocentesis is under a statutory ban; embryo transfer is part of IVF; amniocentesis samples amniotic fluid, not urine.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Reproductive health – problems and strategies
solution.final_answer: Option B: It is based on the chromosomal pattern in the amniotic fluid and can detect genetic disorders such as Down syndrome

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are correct?

(a) Except hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other STIs are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.
(b) Chlamydiasis, trichomoniasis and genital warts are sexually transmitted infections.
(c) If untreated, STIs can lead to pelvic inflammatory disease, ectopic pregnancy and infertility.
(d) The incidence of STIs is reported to be highest in the 45–60 year age group.
(e) Hepatitis-B can be transmitted only through sexual contact.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: STIs include gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B and HIV. All except hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV are completely curable if treated early. Untreated STIs can cause PID, abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancy, infertility or cancer of the reproductive tract. Incidence is highest in the 15–24 year age group. Hepatitis-B and HIV also spread through shared needles, blood transfusion and from mother to foetus.
steps: (d) False: highest in the 15–24 year age group
(e) False: also through shared needles, transfusion and mother to foetus
solution.why_others_wrong: (e) fails because of the word 'only'; (d) gives the wrong age group.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Sexually transmitted infections (STIs)
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Progestogens, progestogen–estrogen combinations or IUDs used within 72 hours of coitus are very effective as emergency contraceptives.
Statement II: In periodic abstinence, couples avoid coitus from day 10 to day 17 of the menstrual cycle, when ovulation could be expected.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements match NCERT: emergency contraception within 72 hours of coitus (for example after rape or casual unprotected intercourse), and periodic abstinence during days 10–17, the fertile period.
solution.why_others_wrong: Students who remember 72 hours as 24 hours, or the fertile period as the menstrual days, wrongly reject one statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population stabilisation and birth control
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A woman cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment in her oviduct for fertilisation and further development of the embryo. Which assisted reproductive technique is designed for such a case?

options.text: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) using her own ova
Zygote intra fallopian transfer (ZIFT) using a zygote formed from her own ovum

solution.explanation: GIFT (gamete intra fallopian transfer) transfers an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation and development.
steps: Problem: no ova, but a functional oviduct
Donor ovum placed in her fallopian tube → GIFT
solution.why_others_wrong: IUI, ICSI and ZIFT with her own ova all need ova from the woman, which she cannot produce.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Infertility
solution.final_answer: Option C: Gamete intra fallopian transfer (GIFT)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In ZIFT, the zygote is transferred into the uterus.
Reason (R): In IUT, embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In embryo transfer after IVF, the zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) is transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT), while embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus (IUT). A is false; R is true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Infertility
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In S.L. Miller's experiment, an electric discharge was passed through a closed flask containing CH₄, H₂, NH₃ and water vapour. He observed the formation of:

solution.explanation: Miller recreated the supposed conditions of early earth on a laboratory scale and observed the formation of amino acids, supporting the idea of chemical evolution (Oparin and Haldane).
steps: Electric discharge + CH₄, H₂, NH₃, water vapour → amino acids
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Origin of life
solution.final_answer: Option B: Amino acids

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs represents analogous structures?

options.text: Forelimbs of a whale and a bat
Wings of a butterfly and wings of a bird

solution.explanation: Analogous structures perform similar functions but are not anatomically similar; they result from convergent evolution. The wings of a butterfly and of a bird are a standard example.
steps: Butterfly wing vs bird wing → analogous
solution.why_others_wrong: Forelimbs, hearts and brains of vertebrates are homologous (same basic structure, divergent evolution).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', What are the evidences for evolution?
solution.final_answer: Option B: Wings of a butterfly and wings of a bird

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Darwin observed many varieties of finches in the Galapagos Islands. From the original seed-eating form, other forms with altered beaks arose, enabling them to become insectivorous and vegetarian. This is an example of:

solution.explanation: Evolution of different species in a given geographical area starting from a point and radiating to other habitats is adaptive radiation; Darwin's finches are the NCERT example.
steps: One ancestral seed-eating finch → many forms with different beaks → adaptive radiation
solution.why_others_wrong: Industrial melanism refers to the peppered moths; saltation is de Vries' single-step large mutation; analogy describes similar function with different structure.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', What is adaptive radiation?
solution.final_answer: Option C: Adaptive radiation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to Darwin, 'fitness' ultimately and only refers to:

options.text: Ability to modify organs by their use and disuse

solution.explanation: Darwinian fitness is reproductive fitness: those better fit in an environment leave more progeny, survive more and are selected by nature.
solution.why_others_wrong: The use-and-disuse option describes Lamarck's idea, not Darwin's.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Biological evolution
solution.final_answer: Option D: Reproductive fitness

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Hugo de Vries proposed the idea of mutations based on his work on the evening primrose.
Statement II: According to de Vries, mutations are small and directional, like the variations that Darwin described.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: de Vries worked on the evening primrose and proposed that mutations (large differences arising suddenly) cause evolution. Mutations are random and directionless, while Darwinian variations are small and directional.
steps: Statement II: false (mutations are random and directionless)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Mechanism of evolution
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, the frequency of allele A is 0.8. The percentage of heterozygous (Aa) individuals in the population is:

solution.explanation: With p = 0.8 the other allele has q = 1 − 0.8 = 0.2. The heterozygote frequency is 2pq.
solution.why_others_wrong: 16% forgets the factor 2 (pq); 64% is p² (AA); 4% is q² (aa).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg principle
solution.final_answer: Option B: 32%

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (hominid) with List-II (feature).

List-I:
A. Homo habilis
B. Homo erectus
C. Neanderthal man
D. Australopithecines

List-II:
I. Brain about 900 cc; probably ate meat
II. Brain about 1400 cc; buried their dead
III. Brain 650–800 cc; probably did not eat meat
IV. Lived in East African grasslands about 2 mya; hunted with stone weapons but essentially ate fruit

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Lichens can be used as industrial pollution indicators.
Reason (R): Lichens do not grow in areas that are polluted.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In the peppered-moth story, white lichens covered tree trunks before industrialisation. NCERT notes that lichens can be used as industrial pollution indicators because they will not grow in polluted areas. R explains A.
steps: Absence of lichens signals pollution → R explains A

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) According to the Hardy-Weinberg principle, allele frequencies in a population are stable and constant from generation to generation unless disturbed.
(b) The sum total of all the allelic frequencies is 1.
(c) When the original drifted population becomes the founders of a new population, the effect is called the founder effect.
(d) Genetic recombination does not affect Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.
(e) Mutation is not one of the factors that affect Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and the factors that disturb it
solution.explanation: The gene pool stays constant (genetic equilibrium) unless disturbed. NCERT lists five disturbing factors: gene migration (gene flow), genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination and natural selection. A drifted population that founds a new one shows the founder effect.
steps: (d) False: recombination is one of the five factors
(e) False: mutation is one of the five factors
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg principle
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: When more than one adaptive radiation appears to have occurred in an isolated geographical area (representing different habitats), it can be called:

solution.explanation: NCERT: when more than one adaptive radiation appears to have occurred in an isolated geographical area, one can call this convergent evolution. Example: Australian placental mammals each resembling a corresponding marsupial (placental wolf and Tasmanian wolf).
steps: Several adaptive radiations in one isolated area → convergent evolution
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', What is adaptive radiation?
solution.final_answer: Option B: Convergent evolution

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a population, natural selection leads to more individuals acquiring peripheral character values at both ends of the distribution curve. This type of natural selection is:

solution.explanation: Natural selection can lead to stabilisation (more individuals near the mean), directional change (more individuals at a value other than the mean) or disruption (more individuals at both peripheral ends).
solution.why_others_wrong: Stabilising favours the mean, directional favours one side; drift is a chance change, not selection.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg principle (operation of natural selection)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Disruptive selection (disruption)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The forelimbs of whales, bats, cheetahs and humans share a similar pattern of bones: humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals and phalanges.
Statement II: Similarities in proteins and genes performing a given function among diverse organisms give clues to common ancestry.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both are NCERT evidences for evolution: homologous forelimbs (same structure developed in different directions by divergent evolution), and biochemical similarity of proteins and genes pointing to common ancestry.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', What are the evidences for evolution?
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A population of 1000 individuals has 500 AA, 400 Aa and 100 aa individuals. What is the frequency of allele a, and how many aa individuals would be expected if the population were in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium with the same allele frequencies?

solution.concept: Allele frequency by gene counting; Hardy-Weinberg expectation
solution.explanation: Count alleles directly: each aa has two a alleles and each Aa has one. The square-root method is valid only when the population is known to be in equilibrium, which is not assumed here.
steps: Expected aa = q² × N = 0.09 × 1000 = 90 (observed is 100, so the population is not in equilibrium)
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.316 takes √(100/1000) as if the population were already in equilibrium; '0.3 and 100' gives the observed rather than the expected number; 0.5 counts every individual carrying a as if it were an allele count.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg principle
solution.final_answer: Option D: 0.3 and 90

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: To release DNA, cells are broken with enzymes that digest their walls: lysozyme (bacteria), cellulase (plant cells) and chitinase (fungi). RNA is removed with ribonuclease and proteins with protease; chilled ethanol then precipitates the purified DNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of recombinant DNA technology (isolation of the genetic material)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When foreign DNA is ligated at the BamHI site of pBR322, the recombinant transformants grow on an ampicillin-containing medium but not on a tetracycline-containing medium.
Reason (R): Insertion of foreign DNA at the BamHI site inactivates the tetracycline resistance gene.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The BamHI site lies in the tetracycline resistance gene of pBR322. Inserting DNA there inactivates tetracycline resistance, while the ampicillin resistance gene stays intact. So recombinants grow on ampicillin but not on tetracycline; non-recombinants grow on both. R explains A.
steps: Loss of tetR (with ampR intact) is exactly why recombinants fail on tetracycline
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology (cloning vectors)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about restriction enzymes are correct?

(a) In EcoRI, the letter 'R' is derived from the name of the bacterial strain.
(b) Exonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA.
(c) The Roman numeral in the name indicates the order in which the enzymes were isolated from that strain of bacteria.
(d) Fragments with sticky ends produced by the same restriction enzyme can be joined by DNA ligase.
(e) A restriction endonuclease cuts only one strand of the DNA double helix.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Naming and action of restriction enzymes
solution.explanation: In EcoRI, 'E' is the genus (Escherichia), 'co' the species (coli), 'R' the strain (RY 13) and 'I' the order of isolation. Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends; endonucleases cut at specific positions within the DNA, cutting both strands. Sticky ends made by the same enzyme are joined by DNA ligase.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology (restriction enzymes)
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Stirred-tank bioreactors are usually cylindrical or have a curved base to facilitate mixing of the reactor contents.
Statement II: Bioreactors can process only small volumes of culture, less than 1 litre.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Bioreactors process large volumes (100–1000 litres) of culture under optimal conditions. The most common are stirred-tank reactors, which are cylindrical or have a curved base for mixing; the stirrer also spreads oxygen evenly.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of recombinant DNA technology (obtaining the foreign gene product)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A recombinant DNA is inserted within the coding sequence of the enzyme β-galactosidase in a vector, and the transformed bacteria are grown on a medium with a chromogenic substrate. Which result is expected?

options.text: Colonies with the insert give blue colour, while colonies without the insert produce no colour
Colonies with the insert produce no colour, while colonies without the insert give blue colour
All colonies give blue colour, whether or not they carry the insert
No colony gives any colour, whether or not it carries the insert

solution.explanation: An insert in the β-galactosidase gene inactivates the enzyme. Colonies whose plasmid has no insert make β-galactosidase and give blue colour with the chromogenic substrate; colonies with the insert produce no colour and are identified as recombinants.
steps: No insert → enzyme active → blue colonies
solution.why_others_wrong: The first wrong option reverses the result: the insert destroys the enzyme, so it cannot produce colour.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology (cloning vectors)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Colonies with the insert produce no colour, while colonies without the insert give blue colour

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A linear DNA molecule and a circular plasmid each have 3 recognition sites for EcoRI. If each is completely digested with EcoRI, the number of fragments obtained from the linear DNA and from the circular plasmid, respectively, will be:

solution.explanation: Each cut in a linear molecule adds one piece, so n cuts give n + 1 fragments. A circle must be cut once just to open it, so n cuts in a circular molecule give n fragments.
solution.why_others_wrong: '3 and 4' swaps the two rules; '4 and 4' treats the plasmid as linear; '3 and 3' treats the linear DNA as circular.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology (restriction enzymes)
solution.final_answer: Option D: 4 and 3

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the cloning vector pBR322 are correct?

(a) The rop gene codes for proteins involved in the replication of the plasmid.
(b) The SalI recognition site lies within the tetracycline resistance gene.
(c) Inserting foreign DNA at the PstI site inactivates tetracycline resistance.
(d) pBR322 carries two antibiotic resistance genes, ampR and tetR.
(e) The rop gene confers resistance to ampicillin.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: pBR322 has ori, rop (proteins for plasmid replication) and two resistance genes, ampR and tetR. The BamHI and SalI sites lie in tetR, while the PstI site lies in ampR, so an insert at PstI inactivates ampicillin resistance, not tetracycline resistance.
steps: (e) False: rop is for replication proteins
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) is the trap: an insert at PstI knocks out ampicillin resistance.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology (cloning vectors, Fig. pBR322)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Continuous culture systems produce a larger biomass, leading to higher yields of the desired protein.
Reason (R): In a continuous culture system, the cells are maintained in their physiologically most active lag phase.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In continuous culture, used medium is drained from one side while fresh medium is added from the other, keeping the cells in their physiologically most active log (exponential) phase. This gives larger biomass and higher yields. A is true; R is false because it names the lag phase.
steps: R: false (cells are kept in the log/exponential phase, not the lag phase)
solution.why_others_wrong: Reading 'lag' as 'log' leads students to option A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of recombinant DNA technology (obtaining the foreign gene product)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Restriction enzymes cut the DNA strand a little away from the centre of the palindrome site, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands.
Statement II: The sticky ends so produced form hydrogen bonds with their complementary cut counterparts, which facilitates the action of DNA ligase.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Cutting off-centre but between the same two bases on both strands leaves single-stranded overhangs (sticky ends). These pair by hydrogen bonds with complementary ends, which helps DNA ligase join the fragments. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology (restriction enzymes)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is the correct sequence of steps in recombinant DNA technology?

options.text: Isolation of DNA → cutting with restriction enzymes → isolation of desired fragment → transfer into host → ligation into vector → culturing host cells → extraction of product
Isolation of DNA → cutting with restriction enzymes → isolation of desired fragment → ligation into vector → transfer into host → culturing host cells → extraction of product
Isolation of DNA → isolation of desired fragment → cutting with restriction enzymes → ligation into vector → transfer into host → culturing host cells → extraction of product
Isolation of DNA → cutting with restriction enzymes → isolation of desired fragment → ligation into vector → culturing host cells → transfer into host → extraction of product

solution.explanation: NCERT lists the steps as: isolation of DNA, fragmentation by restriction endonucleases, isolation of the desired DNA fragment, ligation into a vector, transfer of the recombinant DNA into the host, culturing the host cells on a large scale, and extraction of the desired product.
steps: Isolate DNA → cut → isolate desired fragment → ligate into vector
Transfer into host → culture → extract product
solution.why_others_wrong: The fragment must be cut before it can be isolated, ligated into the vector before transfer, and transferred before the host is cultured.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of recombinant DNA technology
solution.final_answer: Option B: Isolation of DNA → cutting with restriction enzymes → isolation of desired fragment → ligation into vector → transfer into host → culturing host cells → extraction of product

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (feature or vector) with List-II (role).

List-I:
A. Origin of replication (ori)
B. Selectable marker
C. Agrobacterium tumefaciens
D. Disarmed retroviruses

List-II:
I. Helps identify and eliminate non-transformants and selectively permits the growth of transformants
II. Sequence from where replication starts; also controls the copy number of the linked DNA
III. Delivers T-DNA that transforms normal dicot plant cells into tumour cells
IV. Used to deliver desirable genes into animal cells

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: ori is where replication starts and controls copy number. A selectable marker (e.g. an antibiotic resistance gene) separates transformants from non-transformants. Agrobacterium delivers T-DNA into dicot plant cells; its Ti plasmid has been modified into a non-pathogenic vector. Retroviruses, which can make animal cells cancerous, are disarmed and used to deliver genes into animal cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology (cloning vectors)

questions.question_text: The gene that codes for the Bt toxin is named:

steps: Bt toxin → coded by cry genes
solution.why_others_wrong: rop and ori are parts of the pBR322 vector; ADA codes for adenosine deaminase.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological applications in agriculture

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the Bt toxin are correct?

(a) Bacillus thuringiensis forms protein crystals containing a toxic insecticidal protein during a particular phase of its growth.
(b) Most Bt toxins are equally effective against all groups of insects.
(c) The alkaline pH of the insect gut solubilises the crystals and the toxin becomes active.
(d) The activated toxin binds to the surface of midgut epithelial cells and creates pores that cause swelling and lysis of the cells.
(e) Some strains of B. thuringiensis produce proteins that kill lepidopterans, coleopterans and dipterans.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Mode of action of Bt toxin
solution.explanation: B. thuringiensis makes crystals of an insecticidal protein. In the alkaline insect gut the crystals dissolve and the toxin is activated; it binds midgut epithelial cells and creates pores, causing swelling, lysis and death of the insect. Most Bt toxins are insect-group specific, so the gene is chosen according to the crop and target pest.
steps: (b) False: most Bt toxins are insect-group specific
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological applications in agriculture
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (c), (d) and (e) only

Match List-I (use of transgenic animals) with List-II (example).

List-I:
A. Vaccine safety

C. Biological products
D. Study of disease

I. Transgenic mice used to test the safety of the polio vaccine

III. Transgenic models for diseases such as cancer, cystic fibrosis and Alzheimer's
IV. Animals made more sensitive to toxic substances than non-transgenic animals

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Transgenic mice are used to test vaccine safety (e.g. polio vaccine). For toxicity testing, animals are made more sensitive to toxic substances. Rosie (1997) produced human protein-enriched milk with α-lactalbumin. Transgenic models help study diseases such as cancer, cystic fibrosis, rheumatoid arthritis and Alzheimer's.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Bt toxin does not kill the Bacillus thuringiensis bacterium that produces it.
Reason (R): In the bacterium, the Bt toxin protein exists as an inactive protoxin.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why Bt toxin does not harm the bacterium
solution.explanation: The toxin is stored as an inactive protoxin and becomes active only in the alkaline gut of the insect that eats it. So the bacterium is not harmed. R explains A.
steps: Inactive protoxin inside the bacterium → no harm to it → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological applications in agriculture
